the epithelial cells in young leaf tissues of Japanese pepper are responsible for the formation of volatile monoterpenes (β-phellandrene) and sesquiterpentenes (β-caryophyllenes and germacrene-D), and that the formation of these terpenes occurs at a constant rate during the expansion of secretor cavities.

the epithelial cells that surround the secretory cavits of the leaves of Japanese pepper are responsible for biosynthesizing the monoterpenes (β-phellandrene) and sesquiterpeens (β-caryophyllen, and germacrene-D) that accumulate inside these secretory cavities and that are released to the atmosphere.
